---
title: "Experiment 1: benefit of simple-to-complex curricula"
output: html_document
date: "2026-02-16"
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
library(sjPlot)
library(lme4)
library(emmeans)
library(dplyr)
```

```{r define model functions, include=FALSE}
my_tab_model <- function(model){
  tab_model(model, 
          df.method = "wald",
          show.stat=TRUE,
          CSS = list(css.tdata = 'padding:0.1cm;padding-left:0.2cm;padding-right:0.2cm;'),
          transform = NULL,
          string.stat = "z",
          string.p = "p > |z|",
          show.re.var = FALSE,
          show.icc = FALSE,
          show.r2 = FALSE,
          wrap.labels = 100,
          show.ngroups = FALSE,
          show.obs = FALSE)
}

my_plot_model <- function(model){
  plot_model(model, 
          show.intercept = T,
          value.offset = 0.35,
          transform = NULL,
          show.values = T,) + 
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", alpha = .5)
}

scale_this <- function(x){
  (x - mean(x, na.rm=TRUE)) / sd(x, na.rm=TRUE)
}
```

### Loading Data
All continuous variables are z-scored, curriculum is coded as a categorical predictor using treatment (dummy) coding and "No Curriculum" as the reference condition.
```{r read data, echo=T, results='hide', warning=FALSE}
train_data_ctrl <- read_csv("../data/exp1_learning_control.csv",show_col_types = FALSE)
train_data_ctrl$trial_z <- scale_this(train_data_ctrl$trialNum)

test_data_ctrl <- read_csv("../data/exp1_test_control.csv",show_col_types = FALSE)

test_data <- read_csv("../data/exp1_test.csv",show_col_types = FALSE)
test_data$trial_z <- scale_this(test_data$trialNum)
test_data$curriculum <- relevel(
  factor(test_data$curriculum),
  ref = "No\nCurriculum"
)
```

### Humans demonstrate simplicity biases
We first examine learning and test performance in the absence of a curriculum.
```{r train mod }
train_ctrl_mod = glmer(correct ~ stimType * trial_z + (1 | subjectId), 
      data = train_data_ctrl,
      family = binomial,
      control = glmerControl(
        optimizer = "bobyqa",
        optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5)
      ),
      contrasts = list(
      stimType="contr.sum"))
my_tab_model(train_ctrl_mod)

test_ctrl_mod = glmer(correct ~ stimType + (stimType | subjectId), 
                  data = test_data_ctrl,
                  family = binomial,
                  control = glmerControl(
                    optimizer = "bobyqa",
                    optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5)
                  ),
                  contrasts = list(
                  stimType="contr.sum"))
my_tab_model(test_ctrl_mod)

# Per-subject exception accuracy in the first block (blockNum is 0-indexed)
exc_block1 <- train_data_ctrl %>%
  filter(stimType == "Exception", blockNum == min(blockNum)) %>%
  group_by(subjectId) %>%
  summarise(acc = mean(correct), .groups = "drop")

# One-sample t-test against chance
t.test(exc_block1$acc, mu = 0.5)

# Cohen's d
(mean(exc_block1$acc) - 0.5) / sd(exc_block1$acc)
```

### Humans benefit from simple-to-complex curricula
We next test whether curriculum condition affects test performance and whether the effect of curriculum differs by stimulus type.
```{r test mod}
test_mod = glmer(correct ~ curriculum * stimType + (stimType | subjectId), 
                  data = test_data,
                  family = binomial,
                  control = glmerControl(
                    optimizer = "bobyqa",
                    optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5)
                  ),
                  contrasts = list(
                  stimType="contr.sum"))

my_tab_model(test_mod)

# Overall contrasts
emm_overall <- emmeans(
  test_mod,
  ~ curriculum,
  weights = "proportional"
)

# Contrasts separately for exceptions and rules
emm <- emmeans(test_mod, ~ curriculum | stimType)

stim_contrasts <- contrast(
  emm,
  method = list(
    "STC - No Curriculum" = c(-1, 0, 1),
    "CTS - No Curriculum" = c(-1, 1, 0)
  )
)

summary(stim_contrasts, infer = c(TRUE, TRUE))
```
